DialogLine.Default: The Senate does not bind the Empire to a treaty on so short an acquaintance. Patience is a virtue we expect in others.

DialogLine.Friendly: Greetings. We are the Romulan Star Empire. We are pleased to find a people who understand the value of a measured welcome.
DialogLine.Neutral: This is the Romulan Star Empire. We have watched your ships for some time. State your purpose, and be brief.
DialogLine.Hostile: So you have found us. The Romulan Star Empire does not invite strangers to its borders. Choose your next words with care.

DialogLine.Friendly: Our Senate has noted your colony in TARSYS. We are sure it is a misunderstanding, and we are confident you will correct it.
DialogLine.Neutral: SING, your settlement in TARSYS lies within the Empire's interests. We suggest you reconsider before the Tal Shiar does it for you.
DialogLine.Hostile: A colony in TARSYS, in the Empire's sphere? The Praetor has taken note. That was a mistake.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your warships fired upon ours. We assume this was an error among friends. We hope you will make that clear.
DialogLine.Neutral: You have struck at Romulan ships, SING. The Empire has a long memory and a longer reach.
DialogLine.Hostile: You will pay for this aggression, PLURAL. The Empire does not forget, and it does not forgive.

DialogLine.Friendly: Your ships have been near our borders for some time, friend. We would appreciate your withdrawal, before others in the Senate grow concerned.
DialogLine.Neutral: PLURAL ships in Romulan space. We are watching. You may leave in peace, or you may stay and see what we do.
DialogLine.Hostile: Your ships are in Romulan space, PLURAL. Withdraw them at once, or our warbirds will do it for you.

DialogLine.Friendly: We asked you to withdraw from our space, and you did not. Now you have taken TARSYS. We are disappointed.
DialogLine.Neutral: You were told to leave Romulan space, and instead you settled TARSYS. This is a very poor decision, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: You trespassed, you were warned, and now you take TARSYS. The Praetor will answer your insolence.

DialogLine.Friendly: You settled TARSYS, and we kept our silence, and now your fleet crowds our space. Our patience has limits.
DialogLine.Neutral: First TARSYS, and now your warships at our borders. The Empire is beginning to understand your intentions, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: You took TARSYS and now you bring warships to the Empire's door. The Senate will not be patient a third time.

Dialogs.DialogLine: Declare War The Praetor has spoken. The Empire is at war with you. Your worlds will learn what the Romulan Star Empire does to its enemies. Our warbirds are already on their way. You will not see them until it is too late.>

DialogLine.Default: There are others beyond our borders? We have heard rumour of them. The Empire has not yet had the pleasure.

DialogLine.Friendly: Ah, a friend. The Senate is pleased to hear from you. What may the Empire do for you?
DialogLine.Neutral: You have our attention, SING. We trust you will not waste it.
DialogLine.Hostile: Speak. We are listening, though we are not inclined to be generous.

DialogLine.Default: Your people have an interesting history. Tell us how you came to be where you are now.
Interesting. We shall remember it.
No. We do not yet trust you enough for such an agreement.
This is a generous offer from a people we hardly trust. We accept, naturally. We will be watching to see what you hoped to gain by it.
No. The terms are poor, and we do not trust you enough to overlook it.
We have a good opinion of you, so we will be plain: your offer is not good enough. Try again.
A rival holds worlds in that system, and we have no open borders with them. We cannot have your fleet crossing our lines.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: The Empire will choose its own enemies, SING. We do not need yours.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: Outsiders meddling on our borders. We would have expected better manners.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: To set neighbours against each other is a dishonourable game. We are surprised you would try it.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: You would have us quarrel with our neighbours? We would rather talk to them than fight them.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: A clever scheme. The Empire invented most of them, and it will not be played by its own tricks.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: We see the trap you have laid, and we admire the effort. We will not step into it.

DialogLine.Default: The Empire's enemies hold worlds in that system, SING. We will not let you settle in the middle of our war.
DialogLine.DL_Agg: When the Empire wants those worlds, it will take them from our enemies by force.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: The Empire does not need outsiders to settle its battlefields.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: We will not put your settlers in danger on our account. We are grateful for the thought.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: We hope to end that war, not spread it. Thank you, but no.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: Those worlds will be ours soon enough, without your help.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: A world on a front line is a liability, not a prize. Perhaps another time.

DialogLine.Default: This offer is an insult to the Empire. We reject it, and we will remember it.
This is a fair arrangement. The Senate approves. It is agreed.
A good arrangement for both of us. The Senate accepts.
You are far too generous, SING. We accept, and we shall remember your generosity.
A gift. How thoughtful. The Empire accepts it, naturally.
Your request is modest enough. We accept it, and we expect you to remember that we did.
You think the Empire will bend to this? Come and enforce it, if you dare.
Very well. The Empire has no wish to be quarrelsome over a small matter.
A poor bargain, forced upon us. Enjoy it while it lasts. The Empire has a long memory.
You make a pact with the Empire, and then break it? That was unwise. It is war.
So it comes to war. We had prepared for it long ago, and we are quite ready.
We are at war, PLURAL. Whatever you have to say, say it quickly.
You bring your ships to our border, so our warbirds will meet them. Let us see which of us was better prepared.
We told you not to enter Romulan territory, and you did it anyway. The Senate has chosen war.
You remain in TARSYS despite our warnings, PLURAL. The Empire is now at war with you.
The Empire would prefer to avoid needless conflict. Perhaps a non-aggression pact would serve us both?
A sensible choice. The Empire will honour this agreement, as long as you do.
You refuse? The offer will not remain open indefinitely. We suggest you reconsider.
The Senate has considered the matter of trade, and the Empire is willing to open its markets to you. Shall we draw up a treaty?
Excellent. May our exchange be profitable for both our peoples.
You decline the Empire's offer of trade. We are surprised, SING, and we will not forget it.
First you declined a pact, and now you ask for one? The Senate does not appreciate indecision.
You refused trade before. Now you ask for it. We would like to know what has changed.
The Empire requires TECH_DEMAND from you, SING. We would hate for our relations to suffer.
Thank you. The Empire appreciates a sensible partner.
You refuse? How unwise. We will remember this, SING.
The PLURAL fleet is a curiosity. We would pity you, but the Empire has no use for pity.
Your fleet is not unimpressive. The Empire notes it, with some interest.
You have strengthened your fleet, SING. We will have to adjust our plans accordingly.
You are too weak to hold your worlds, SING. The Empire will gladly take them off your hands.
The Kulrathi Shogunate has a proper respect for order and discipline. We have much in common with them.
The Kulrathi keep to their warrior's code. We neither trust them nor fear them. A suitable arrangement.
The Kulrathi believe their code makes them wiser than us. The Empire has been listening to such claims for centuries.
The Pollops are gentle and well mannered. They are no threat, and they have lovely songs. We wish them well.
The Pollops live quietly among their gardens. They are no concern of the Empire, and we have no concern with them.
The Pollops are too naive to survive for long. The Empire would be doing them a kindness to take charge of their worlds.
The Vulfen Imperium is proud and fierce. We can respect an empire that knows what it is. We are on good terms.
The Vulfen Imperium is loud and warlike. They have not troubled us, and we have taken care not to trouble them.
The Vulfen Imperium is a pack of loud, aggressive hunters, and they mistake noise for strength. We will teach them otherwise.
The Humans are an unpredictable people, and we find that refreshing. They have a gift for surprising us. We like them for it.
The Humans are a young people, loud and idealistic. They have not yet harmed the Empire, and we have no strong view.
The Humans speak of peace, and they call it a virtue. They have yet to learn how it is kept. We do not care to teach them.
The Ralyeh Devoted are patient and committed to their ways. We know a good deal about patience. We approve of theirs.
The Ralyeh pray to their gods and keep to their own waters. The Empire does not meddle in faith, as long as faith does not meddle with us.
The Ralyeh Devoted speak of their gods and their dead. Those who worship death should not be surprised to meet it.
You thought a treaty would hold the Empire? Treaties are tools, SING. This one has served its purpose.
The game is done, SING. The Empire has won, and your worlds are ours. The Praetor thanks you for your cooperation.
The PLURAL have behaved with propriety, and the Senate sees no harm in open borders. Shall we agree to it?
A wise decision. Our ships may pass in peace, and we expect yours to do the same.
You refuse open borders? Then we shall continue to look at you from afar. For now.
We had a treaty, and you broke it. The Senate will not forget this betrayal. We are at war.
TARSYS is Romulan territory. You have invaded it. The Empire is now at war with you.
The Opteris are efficient, patient and not given to idle talk. We admire that.
The Opteris are an odd people, half machine and half insect. We keep watch on them, as we do on everyone.
The Opteris are cold and mechanical, and they cannot be bargained with. It makes them a danger, and the Empire dislikes dangers.

DialogLine.Friendly: Dear friend, the Empire has claimed TARSYS. We would be grateful if you would not settle there.
DialogLine.Neutral: TARSYS is claimed by the Empire. We suggest you look elsewhere, SING.
DialogLine.Hostile: TARSYS is within the Empire's claim, PLURAL. Settle there, and we will remove you.

DialogLine.Default: TARSYS was claimed by the Empire. You took it. The Senate does not overlook such things.
We have only just made your acquaintance, PLURAL. We are still forming our opinion.
We have no quarrel with the PLURAL. You have been courteous, and the Senate takes note.
We have some concerns about you, PLURAL. We shall be happy to discuss them, at length.
You have taken worlds that the Empire had its eye on. This is noticed.
You have taken worlds that the Empire had its eye on. This is noticed.
Your fleet has grown too large for comfort. The Senate is considering what that means.
Your fleet is small, and a weak neighbour is a temptation. We would prefer not to be tempted.
Your fleet is weak. The Empire does not make alliances with the defenceless.
Your fleet has grown too large for comfort. The Senate is considering what that means.
You are allied with TAREMP, who are enemies of the Empire. A curious choice of friends.
You remain allied with TAREMP, who are enemies of the Empire. We have noted it.
We have no great quarrel with you. We would like it to stay that way.
The war goes well for the Empire, SING. You may wish to speak, while there is still someone to listen.
The war has not gone as the Senate had hoped. We are willing to hear you, SING.
TAREMP are enemies of the Empire. We invite you to fight beside us. There will be rewards for those who help.
Excellent. The Senate will remember this. Together we shall crush TAREMP.
You decline to help us against TAREMP? The Empire will remember who stood with it, and who did not.
We trusted our treaty, and you broke it. The Empire will make sure you regret it.
This war has cost us both enough. The Senate would be willing to discuss peace.
We are winning this war, but the Senate sees no profit in prolonging it. Make peace with us.
Neither of us can win this war, SING. A sensible people would end it before more ships are lost.
The war has gone badly for us. We would be willing to make peace, on reasonable terms.
We hold your worlds. Sign this treaty, and the war will end.
You hold the field, SING. Keep your worlds, and give us peace. The Empire will bide its time.
You refuse peace? Then we continue. The Empire is patient.
Very well. There will be peace between us. The Senate is satisfied.
A reasonable offer. The Senate accepts. There will be peace between us.
Your offer is not good enough. There will be no peace on those terms.
You still hold worlds that the Empire wants. There will be no peace.
We will accept this peace, though it does not please us. Do not mistake it for friendship.
We were at war not long ago. The Senate has not forgotten, and neither should you.
The Empire and the PLURAL have a good understanding of each other. Perhaps it is time for a formal alliance.
Excellent. The Senate welcomes this alliance, and looks forward to its fruits.
You decline an alliance with the Empire? Perhaps you will think again.
This is needlessly complicated. If you wish an alliance, propose one plainly.
The Senate agrees. The Empire will stand with you, as long as you stand with us.
An alliance? The Empire has not yet decided that you deserve one.
No peace. The Empire intends to finish what it has begun.
There has been no great loss on either side. A sensible time to make peace. The Senate agrees.
You will not fight beside us? Then you are no ally of the Empire. The alliance is ended.
You have crossed the Empire twice now. A third time would be unwise.
You have stolen from the Empire too many times. The Praetor's patience is at an end.

DialogLine.DL_Agg: The Romulan Star Empire does not seek war. It simply prepares for it, as any prudent people must, and the Senate is always prepared.
DialogLine.DL_Hon: Our people hold honour above comfort, and duty above life. We expect the same of those who deal with us.
DialogLine.DL_Pac: The Empire would prefer peace, and has often kept it. But a wise people do not mistake peace for weakness, and neither should you.
DialogLine.DL_Ruth: The Romulan people have survived by being more patient and more thorough than their enemies. The Empire will go on surviving.
DialogLine.DL_Xeno: The Romulan people have kept apart from the galaxy for a very long time. We see no reason to change.
DialogLine.DL_Cunn: A people who tell you everything they know have nothing left to trade. We prefer to keep a little in reserve.
DialogLine.DL_Exp: The Empire's borders are wide, and its ambitions wider. There is always another world worth the Senate's attention.
DialogLine.DL_Tech: Our science is well advanced, and our engineers have never been shy about using it. Do not be surprised by what we can build.
DialogLine.DL_Mil: Our warbirds are the finest in the quadrant. Many have learned this at too late a moment.
DialogLine.DL_Ind: The Empire's shipyards are busy, and its people disciplined. Nothing is wasted.
DialogLine.DL_Gen: The Empire is old, patient and proud. We take the long view, and we have rarely been surprised by what it shows.

DialogLine.Default: The Cordrazine Collective is orderly and disciplined. We can respect a people who keep their house in order.
We know the Cordrazine only a little. They keep to themselves, which we find sensible.
The Cordrazine hide behind their Collective and speak with one voice. We prefer to know who is speaking.
We know that you are spying on us, SING. We are flattered, but we ask that you stop.
We asked you to stop spying. The Tal Shiar does not ask twice.
You have spied on us again. All treaties between our peoples are cancelled.
We have captured your spy. He told us a great deal, and then a little more.
Caught in the act of espionage? How quaint. Better luck next time.
A spy among our allies? We caught your agent. Is this how the PLURAL treat friends?
You spy on us again, ally? Our alliance is at an end.
Friends should not keep their borders closed to each other. Open yours to us, SING.
You keep your borders closed even to friends? The PLURAL are very careful.
We have only just met. The Senate does not join a federation with strangers.
We are not even allies. The Senate will not consider a federation until we are.
We are allies, and it is a good beginning. But a federation requires a longer history of trust.
Why should the Empire follow you? We are the stronger power. If anything, you should join us.
Our peoples have come far, SING. The Senate has agreed. We will stand together in a federation, and face what comes.
Before we join you, the Empire asks a service. Destroy TAREMP, and we will consider it.
TAREMP is destroyed. The Senate is satisfied. The Empire will join your federation.
You wish us to join your federation? The Empire does not even trust you.
We will join you, but you must first become allies with our friends, TAREMP. Win their confidence, and speak to us again.
You have made allies of our friends. The Senate is pleased. The Empire will join your federation.
You are not even at war with TAREMP. Why would the Empire fight for you?
The Empire is already at war with TAREMP. Were you not informed?
The Empire stands with its allies. We will make war on TAREMP, and the Praetor will see it done.
TAREMP is our ally. The Empire does not break its word, even for a friend. We regret it.
Why should the Empire fight for you, PLURAL? Our relations do not warrant such a favour.
The Empire has no appetite for war with TAREMP. We would prefer to settle our differences without bloodshed.
TAREMP is formidable. The Senate does not choose such a war lightly. We decline.
We agree to your proposal. Much can be gained in a war with TAREMP. Save some worlds for the Empire.
The Senate is concerned that you cannot be trusted as an ally, SING. We would like to see that change.
The Senate has revoked our open borders. We no longer trust your empire to keep them.
